- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and prices are trending down, model often overpredicts recovery; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated upward momentum; cap forecast growth at 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4) and prices show mean reversion, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing filter or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price surges (especially post-2024-10); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- When sentiment is low but price is rising, model often ignores sentiment and overpredicts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment <0.2 and price > previous 3-day high.
